title: How to sort
lede: What to keep, where it goes, and checking the rewrites.

slides.cap: Keep what helps someone make or study education policy. Delete the rest, and keep each thing once.

notes.html: The line at the top then says where it waits next.
Undo is on the line at the top, and on the greyed row at the bottom of the list.

slides.cap: About two in five papers, events and opportunities are kept, and one headline in five. An issue wants 3 to 5 outside research items or reports and 3 to 5 headlines.

steps.title: Keep when
items: The research tests a policy, such as teacher pay, attendance or pre-K.
A headline reports a decision, a number or a finding, usually from a state or the federal government.
A local story shows a wider trend: “Oklahoma School Closures Part of Statewide Picture of Enrollment Decline”.
A policy webinar comes from a think tank or research group.
It is an ERC event or an A&M research talk.
It offers education researchers money, a fellowship or a call for proposals, with the deadline ahead.
A person added it: their initials or name follow added by (bulk upload means none were given). Keep it unless it repeats.

slides.cap: Delete it when any of these is true.

steps.title: Delete when
items: It is not about education.
It is one bill or one rule notice.
It is campus news, a scandal or a celebrity. College news that is state policy stays.
It is one district's news with no wider point: “Austin ISD faces deeper budget cuts as enrollment declines”.
It is opinion, an interview, a podcast, a guide or a roundup.
A webinar teaches classroom practice or sells something.
It is a job, an award or a conference listing. Grants with no deadline or for another field go too.
The research has no policy in it: a method, a theory or a program description.
It is a repeat. Keep the best copy.

slides.cap: Some sources have a clear rule, from how often they were kept.

steps.title: A clear rule
items: ECS State Policy Tracker, 0 of 54 kept: delete. Each is one state bill.
Austin American-Statesman, 0 of 24: delete. Austin ISD and UT campus news.
Urban Institute, 6 of 41: delete unless it is about schools.
NBER, 3 of 18: delete unless it is about schooling.
K-12 Dive, 6 of 17: keep findings and state counts. Delete Week In Review.
EdWorkingPapers, 32 of 58: keep most. Delete methods papers.

steps.title: Nearly every time
items: Kept: CALDER, Texas Tribune, the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board, the Tennessee Education Research Alliance, and ERC and A&M events.
Deleted: Texas Public Radio, KUT, PBS NewsHour, the Department of Education newsroom, the Federal Register, WestEd and AIR.

slides.cap: Leave ERC Newsletter only unticked for most items. Tick it to keep one off the Policy Exchange.

notes.html: Give ERC events the ERC event type. They go everywhere.
The desk ticks the box for any Event with the A&M subtype.
Tick it for a notice meant for a small campus audience. Untick it for an A&M talk by an education policy researcher.

slides.cap: A triangle in the list means the card has a question. Keep and next waits until the type and the link are settled.

notes.html: After Verify link, press Confirm if the page is right, or Change to paste the right link.
Possible duplicate names the earlier item. Not every repeat shows it.

slides.cap: Not sure? Press Skip for now. Clear Past and Already live with Dismiss all; one Undo brings a group back.
Kept events, ERC events, opportunities, reports and research with no abstract get a description in the ERC's voice. Check each one here before it goes out.

notes.html: The rewrite starts when you keep, so most arrive on their own.

slides.cap: A rewrite that is back waits under To check, its changed words marked.

steps.title: Check each rewrite
items: Press Keep to use it, or Use original for the text it came with.
Fix a word with Edit. Saving the edit counts as checked.
Keep the rest (N) keeps every rewrite still to check.
